newsitem.title: UK: EBRD backs Bulgaria's Storco with equity, loan.
newsitem.headline: EBRD backs Bulgaria's Storco with equity, loan.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said on Friday it was making a $1.75 million equity investment in Bulgaria's Storco AD and extending it an $8.25 million loan.
The news will be welcomed in Sofia, where the government is closing down a number of loss-making firms and speeding up privatisation to trigger the release of a delayed IMF loan.
Storco is one of the country's biggest food processing companies, and the EBRD said the funding would support its future investment plans.

"The funding will enable Storco to finance its post-privatisaion investment programme, which includes the upgrading of its food-processing facilities, restructuring of its operations and the improvement of its raw material supplies," the bank said in a statement released in London.
Privatised in November 1995 through the sale of 80 percent of its share capital, Storco is involved mainly in the production of processed fruit and vegetables.
The EBRD said its financing would enable Storco to expand its export business while giving a boost to the local economy.

"The bank is confident that Storco will stimulate, directly and indirectly, the local agribusiness sector, which has traditionally been a competitive segment of the Bulgarian economy," said Olivier Descamps, director of the EBRD's Bulgaria team.

"The company will be in a position to demonstrate the potential of the Bulgarian agribusiness sector, which is currently being privatised, and thus attract domestic and foreign investors to an area in need of capital," the statement added.
